errors.description: The pressed front leg crease sits a little outboard of the pleat fold at the top of the leg and converges into it further down, rather than running as one continuous line out of the pleat from the waistband. Both legs behave identically so the pleat still reads cleanly.
errors.expected: Front crease running straight out of the pleat fold from the waistband to the hem as a single line.
errors.actual: Crease and pleat fold offset by roughly a quarter of the pleat depth at the waistband, merging by mid-thigh.
errors.correction: Cosmetic pressing detail; within photographic tolerance and no regeneration warranted.

lockedFeatures: front view of the trousers from waistband to knee
exactly ONE pleat per leg — two pleat mouths in total, one each side of the fly
both pleats folded FORWARD, opening inward toward the fly, mirrored left and right
pleat positioned roughly midway between the fly and the side seam, a little nearer the fly
fly front with topstitched curve, waistband and belt loops
on-seam / slanted side pocket opening at each hip
solid charcoal fine-wool trouser cloth with visible weave
NO magnified circle callout, no annotation ring, no leader line, no text, no numbers, no red marks
notes: Attempt 1. Matches the drawing: trouser front, exactly one pleat per leg, both mirrored and both folded toward the fly (the pleat mouth's shadow wedge faces the centre front on each leg, which is the forward-pleat signature and the opposite of a reverse pleat), pleat placed at about 45% of the distance from the fly to the side seam on each side, matching the red pleat markers in the illustration almost exactly. Pleat depth and the fall of the crease to the knee follow the drawing. Critically, the illustration's magnified circle callout at the top left — a pink annotation ring with a leader line down to the pleat, showing the fold direction — did NOT leak into the photograph; there is no ring, no leader line, no red mark and no text anywhere in the frame, and the red pleat markers were correctly read as position notation and rendered in the garment's own charcoal cloth. Only a small pressing imperfection was found, logged as minor.
